abla_2)\). Vanishing of \([L_1,L_2]\) for every \(\lambda\) gives the three self-duality equations in the corresponding orientation. One cannot change the relative minus sign without changing the real structure or signature.
fate: \citet[\S5 and references7--8]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} identify the Belavin--Zakharov construction used in the notes. The corrected explicit pair is checked by expanding the polynomial commutator, not read into the differently signed P000732 display.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Orthogonal complex structures and the twistor fibration
notes: All linear complex structures on \(\mathbb R^4\) are said to be parameterized by one complex parameter, and \(S^7\to\mathbb CP^3\to S^4\) is drawn.
statement: The orientation-compatible orthogonal complex structures on a Euclidean four-space form \(SO(4)/U(2)\cong S^2\cong\mathbb CP^1\). All linear complex structures form a larger space. The twistor projection \(\mathbb CP^3\to\mathbb HP^1\cong S^4\) has fiber \(\mathbb CP^1\); it factors the quaternionic Hopf map through the circle quotient \(S^7\to\mathbb CP^3\).
fate: The twistor construction is the setting of \citet{atiyahward1977instantons} and \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The notebook omits orthogonality and prints an inconsistent \(\mathbb CP^2\) fiber near the bottom of P000733.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Instantons as holomorphic bundles on twistor space
notes: The connection lifts to \(\mathbb CP^3\), defining an almost complex structure which is integrable precisely under the duality equations.
statement: The pullback of a unitary anti-self-dual connection to twistor space defines an integrable \(\bar\partial\)-operator. For the inverse correspondence one requires a holomorphic bundle trivial on every real twistor line and a compatible real or quaternionic structure with positivity. An arbitrary holomorphic bundle on \(\mathbb CP^3\) does not determine a unitary instanton.
fate: \citet[abstract]{atiyahward1977instantons} state the instanton/holomorphic-bundle identification; \citet[\S5]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} explicitly use this theorem in proving completeness. The full list of reality and line-triviality hypotheses is a modern reconstruction of the terse notes.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Integrability is involutivity of the complex tangent distribution
notes: An almost complex structure is described by local vector fields, which are required to commute.
statement: For a smooth almost complex structure \(J\), integrability is equivalent to involutivity \([T^{0,1},T^{0,1}]\subset T^{0,1}\), or vanishing Nijenhuis tensor. In holomorphic coordinates there is a commuting local frame, but an arbitrary frame of an integrable distribution need not commute. The base \(S^4\) is not thereby given a global complex structure.
fate: The notebook is invoking the classical complex integrability criterion in its twistor application; \citet[\S5]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} rely on the resulting holomorphic-bundle correspondence. This reference is thematic for the general criterion, not a claimed original proof of it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Bounded analytic and inner functions
notes: \(H^\infty\) is the algebra of bounded analytic functions on the disk; inner functions have boundary modulus one almost everywhere.
statement: \(H^\infty(\mathbb D)\) consists of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disk. An inner function has radial boundary values of modulus one for Lebesgue-almost every boundary point. The notation means \(|u(e^{it})|=1\), not multiplication of \(u\) by \(e^{it}\).
fate: \citet[\S1, opening definitions]{sznagy1976diagonalization} use precisely this setting, before the November 1977 talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Canonical factorization and the singular inner factor
notes: A bounded analytic function is decomposed as an inner factor times an outer factor, and the inner factor as a Blaschke product times an exponential built from a singular measure.
statement: Every nonzero \(u\in H^\infty\) has an inner--outer factorization. Its inner part is, up to a unimodular constant, a Blaschke product times \(S_\mu(z)=\exp\{-\int_{0}^{2\pi}(e^{it}+z)(e^{it}-z)^{-1}\,d\mu(t)\}\), for a finite positive singular measure \(\mu\). A positive exponent with positive measure gives the reciprocal and is generally unbounded.
fate: \citet[\S1 and the proof of Lemma~2]{sznagy1976diagonalization} invoke canonical factorization. The minus sign omitted in the notebook is mathematically necessary for the stated class.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Greatest common inner divisor
notes: The wedge \(\bigwedge_\alpha u_\alpha\) is described by a product over zeros and the lower bound of the singular measures.
statement: The greatest common inner divisor of a family of nonzero bounded analytic functions is determined, up to a unimodular factor, by the minimum zero multiplicities at each point and the greatest common lower bound of the singular measures of their inner factors. Zeros belonging to only one member do not contribute. For an all-zero family a separate convention is needed.
fate: \citet[\S1]{sznagy1976diagonalization} explicitly define the divisor for \(H^\infty\) families and use the all-zero value zero.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Failure of an unrestricted Bézout identity in H-infinity
notes: The notes deny that the greatest common inner divisor always has the form \(xu+yv\) with \(x,y\in H^\infty\).
statement: Having no common nonconstant inner divisor does not imply that \(xu+yv=1\) has bounded analytic solutions. Such an identity forces \(\inf_{z\in\mathbb D}(|u(z)|+|v(z)|)>0\), a condition stronger than inner coprimality. Thus \(H^\infty\) is not a Bézout domain in this sense.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S3]{sznagy1976diagonalization} explain why ordinary matrix equivalence must be replaced by quasi-equivalence. This supports the algebraic obstruction; the notebook gives no explicit counterexample.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The stronger outer-factor denial is not a complete statement
notes: A second denied identity has an outer factor \(h\) on one side and a heavily crossed-out mark on the other.
statement: The visible formula suggests a proposed Bézout identity after multiplication by an outer function, but its quantifiers, the crossed-out coefficient, and whether the factor is required to be invertible are not fixed. An exact strengthened negative assertion cannot be supplied responsibly.
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma~2]{sznagy1976diagonalization} give the precise weaker generic-combination statement used next, but do not identify this damaged displayed denial.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, only the following Sherman lemma is securely identified; the stronger denial remains ambiguous.

title: Sherman’s generic linear-combination lemma
notes: For a fixed inner function \(\omega\), constants can be chosen so that \(u+tv=h_t(u\wedge v)\), with \(h_t\wedge\omega=1\); at most countably many \(t\) are exceptional.
statement: Let \(u,v\in H^\infty\) be not both zero, let \(d=u\wedge v\) and let \(\omega\) be inner. After writing \(u=da\), \(v=db\), the functions \(a,b\) have no common nonconstant inner divisor. For all but at most countably many complex \(t\), \(\omega\wedge(a+tb)=1\). Consequently \(u+tv=d h_t\) with \(h_t\wedge\omega=1\). Applying the lemma to the normalized pair is essential; the unnormalized identity \(\omega\wedge(u+tv)=\omega\wedge u\wedge v\) alone is a weaker statement.
fate: Exactly \citet[\S1, Lemma~2, pp.224--225]{sznagy1976diagonalization}, credited there to M. Sherman. The paper was received 1 November 1975 and published in 1976, so the talk is expository.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Finite polynomial combinations and simultaneous rows
notes: The notes extend the lemma to \(u_1+t u_2+\cdots+t^{r-1}u_{r+1}\), and then to finitely many rows.
statement: For a finite list \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\), divide by its common inner divisor. For any fixed inner \(\omega\), the polynomial combination \(u_1+t u_2+\cdots+t^{r-1}u_r\) is then inner-coprime to \(\omega\) outside a countable set of \(t\). One may avoid the union of the exceptional sets for finitely or countably many such rows. The last subscript in the notebook must be \(r\), not \(r+1\).
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma~2 and \S2, Main Lemma]{sznagy1976diagonalization} establish the generic-combination mechanism and a stronger simultaneous \(\ell^1\)-coefficient theorem. The exact moment-curve wording in the notebook is a finite version; the paper\textquotesingle s Main Lemma does not insist on coefficients \(1,t,t^2,\ldots\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Matrix reduction by controlled inner divisors
notes: The final line mentions elementary transformations of a matrix.
statement: The generic-combination lemma can select combinations of rows or columns with prescribed common inner divisors and supports a quasi-equivalence diagonalization theory for finite and semi-finite \(H^\infty\)-matrices. It does not provide a Smith normal form under arbitrary invertible \(H^\infty\) row and column operations, nor settle all doubly infinite matrices.
fate: \citet[\S3]{sznagy1976diagonalization} carry out this program and explicitly separate the convergence difficulty for doubly infinite matrices. The notebook does not itself pose that larger question.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The KP normalization in the notes
notes: The equation is \(\frac34u_{yy}+\partial_x\{u_t+\frac14(6uu_x+u_{xxx})\}=0\).
statement: The recorded equation is \(3u_{yy}+(4u_t+6uu_x+u_{xxx})_x=0\), over complex variables when rational poles are considered. Rescalings or imaginary changes of \(y\) change the sign and strength of the corresponding particle interaction.
fate: The equation is already part of the earlier integrable-equation theory; see \citet[\S1, KP example]{krichever1977methods}. \citet[\S3]{krichever1978rational} print this normalization in the rational-pole context. The latter paper was received 6 September 1977 and appeared in the first issue of 1978; receipt is not by itself evidence of public circulation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The double-pole form of rational decaying KP solutions
notes: Every rational solution decreasing as \(x\to\infty\) is written as \(-2\sum_i(x-x_i(y,t))^{-2}\).
statement: On a parameter domain where poles are distinct, a rational KP solution tending to zero as \(x\to\infty\) has only double poles, zero simple-pole coefficients and leading coefficient \(-2\): \(u=-2\sum_{i=1}^N(x-q_i(y,t))^{-2}\). The pole coordinates can collide at exceptional parameters; a global assertion must allow the resulting limiting rational function.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~3]{krichever1978rational} give the rational-solution characterization together with the associated Baker--Akhiezer function.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The particle Hamiltonian needs a normalization correction
notes: The \(y\)-motion is assigned to \(H=\frac12\sum p_i^2+\sum_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)^{-2}\).
statement: For precisely the displayed KP equation, the ansatz \(u=-2\sum(x-q_i)^{-2}\), and canonical momenta \(p_i=q_{i,y}\), Laurent coefficients give \(q_{i,yy}=-8\sum_{j\ne i}(q_i-q_j)^{-3}\). Thus one consistent canonical Hamiltonian is \(H=\frac12\sum p_i^2-4\sum_{i<j}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\). Other standard Calogero conventions follow by rescaling or complexifying time and momenta; they must be stated.
reconstruction: The canonical convention \(p=q_y\) and the corrected coefficient are an editorial Laurent calculation. A different convention might explain the speaker\textquotesingle s numerical coefficient, but none is recorded.
fate: The pole correspondence is established by \citet[\S2, Theorem~2; \S3, Corollary~1]{krichever1978rational}. Their Hamiltonian notation must be compared together with their time and Poisson conventions; no claim of an error in that published theorem is made here. The displayed notebook equation, ansatz and canonical convention \(p=q_y\) give the coefficients in the statement by direct Laurent expansion.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The KP time is a higher commuting particle flow
notes: The \(t\)-dependence is governed by a second commuting integral of the same particle system.
statement: In the same canonical convention, pole cancellation gives \(q_{i,t}=\frac34p_i^2-3\sum_{j\ne i}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\). It is the position component of the flow generated by \(K=\frac14\sum_i p_i^3-3\sum_{i<j}(p_i+p_j)(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\), which commutes with the Hamiltonian of the preceding item. These compatible flows reconstruct the rational KP solutions where poles remain distinct.
reconstruction: The normalized Hamiltonian \(K\) is an editorial rewriting of the cubic flow; the notebook only names the additional commuting integral.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~3 and Corollary~1]{krichever1978rational} identify the higher flow by a cubic trace invariant. The explicit coefficients here retain the notebook\textquotesingle s KP signs and canonical momenta rather than silently using a differently normalized \(F_3\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The differential-operator compatibility representation
notes: The notes write \(L_1=\partial_x^2+u\), \(L_2=\partial_x^3+\frac32u\partial_x+u\), and a zero-curvature relation.
statement: One consistent pair for the notebook\textquotesingle s KP normalization is \(L=\partial_x^2+u\), \(M=\partial_x^3+\frac32u\partial_x+w\), with \(w=\frac34u_x+\frac34\partial_x^{-1}u_y\), and \([\partial_y-L,\partial_t+M]=0\). The integration constant in \(\partial_x^{-1}u_y\) is fixed by boundary conditions or absorbed in a scalar gauge. The lower coefficient of the third-order operator is a new function \(w\), not simply \(u\).
reconstruction: The coefficient \(w\) and time sign are supplied by direct compatibility; the source has insufficient normalization information to infer them silently.
fate: The compatibility method and KP example already occur in \citet[Theorem~1]{krichever1976zakharov} and \citet[\S1]{krichever1977methods}. \citet[\S3]{krichever1978rational} use a separate scalar coefficient \(w\) in the rational-pole setting. The displayed pair is normalized directly to the notebook equation; the modern verification is not dated as a new 1978 theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Commutative subalgebras of Weyl skew fields
notes: A final proposal concerns commutative subalgebras of \(D_n\), the skew field associated with the Weyl algebra.
statement: The fragment suggests studying commutative subalgebras or subfields inside a Weyl skew field by spectral geometry. It specifies neither a class of subalgebras, a rank, a maximality condition, nor an equivalence relation; it is not a stated classification theorem for all \(n\).
fate: \citet{drinfeld1977commutative} is a contemporary primary lead, received 14 April 1976 and published in 1977, but its title and metadata alone do not verify a general Weyl-skew-field assertion. The notebook proposal remains too short to assign an exact fate.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, no definite new problem with specified quantifiers can be extracted from this fragment.

title: Curvature and the self-duality equations
notes: Manin starts with skew-Hermitian matrix potentials, their curvature, and the equations \(F_{\mu\nu}=\varepsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}F_{\rho\sigma}\).
statement:
For a unitary connection \(
abla=d+A\), \(F=dA+A\wedge A\). In an oriented Euclidean four-manifold the self-duality equation is \(F=*F\), or \(F_{\mu
u}= rac12\sum_{ho,\sigma}\varepsilon_{\mu
uho\sigma}F_{ho\sigma}\). The factor is absent only if one sums over a single complementary ordered pair.
reconstruction: The summation convention is supplied explicitly; the notebook first discusses complementary pairs and then suppresses the convention in its epsilon formula.
fate: This is the established differential-geometric setting recalled in \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. Its use in the later classification does not make the definition a new 1978 result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Gauge changes and removable frame singularities
notes: Changing a local frame gives \(A\mapsto u^{-1}du+u^{-1}Au\); apparent finite-point singularities are required to disappear in a suitable gauge. The covariant-derivative sum incorrectly repeats \(i\) as its summation index.
statement: In a local unitary frame, \(\nabla_\mu s_i=\sum_j A_\mu^{ij}s_j\), with a consistent row or column convention. Smoothness is a property of the connection on the bundle, not of one singular trivialization. Gauge equivalence preserves curvature up to conjugation and preserves self-duality.
fate: \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} formulate regularity and equivalence in terms of bundles with connections. The displayed gauge law is standard; the index repair is elementary and scan-confirmed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Regularity at infinity and compactification
notes: The connection and its bundle must extend over \(S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}\); the extended bundle may be nontrivial.
statement: A regular instanton here means a smooth unitary self-dual connection on a bundle over the round four-sphere, expressed on the affine chart \(\mathbb R^4\). Extension over infinity is an imposed regularity condition in this talk. It should not be confused with a proof that arbitrary finite-action fields extend.
fate: This is precisely the sphere formulation in \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The separate removable-singularity theorem is treated under record 432.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Clutching classification and charge
notes: Clutching along the equator gives \(\pi_3(U(r))=\mathbb Z\), generated by the block embedding of \(SU(2)\), and the sign of charge is reversed with duality.
statement: For \(r\geq2\), complex rank-\(r\) bundles over \(S^4\) are classified by an integer clutching class in \(\pi_3(U(r))\), equivalently the second Chern number after fixing orientation. For \(r=1\), \(\pi_3(U(1))=0\). This classifies underlying bundles, not their connections; a fixed charge supports a moduli space of instantons.
fate: \citet[\S1 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} use the charge \(n\) and rank \(r\) as discrete parameters. The omitted rank-one exception and the distinction from gauge equivalence are essential.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Projection from a finite-dimensional trivial bundle
notes: The announced construction places \(L\) inside \(H\times S^4\), with \(\dim H=2n+r\), and obtains the connection by differentiating and orthogonally projecting.
statement: For the admissible instanton data described below, \(H\times S^4=L\oplus L^\perp\), with \(\operatorname{rank}L=r\), and \(\nabla s=P_L(ds)\). A Hermitian orthogonal projection gives a unitary connection. The sharp ambient dimension and the self-duality conditions belong to the instanton construction, not to an arbitrary connection embedding theorem.
fate: \citet[\S3 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} give this construction; the announcement was received 27 November 1977, six days after the source date, and published in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Can every connection be induced from a trivial one?
notes: A bracketed question asks whether a bundle with connection can always be embedded into a trivial bundle with connection, comparing this with a Euclidean embedding of a Riemannian manifold.
statement: For a smooth Hermitian vector bundle over a finite-dimensional smooth manifold and a compatible unitary connection, does there exist a finite-dimensional trivial Hermitian bundle and an isometric bundle embedding for which orthogonal projection of the trivial connection is the prescribed connection?
reconstruction: The unitary compatibility and finite-dimensional smooth-base assumptions make the intended projection question precise.
fate: Affirmative before the talk: \citet[p.286, universal-connection theorem and the unitary case]{narasimhan1962universal} announce the joint Narasimhan--Ramanan theorem at the September 1961 Prague symposium; the proceedings appeared in 1962. The universal Stiefel connection gives exactly the projection formulation. Earlier occurrence 1975-382.5 describes the tautological universal connection and its base; it has no earlier problem identifier. That construction and this explicit universality question are closely related, with the quantifiers stated here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Quaternionic real structure and the twistor projection
notes: The map \(\sigma(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4)=(-\bar z_2,\bar z_1,-\bar z_4,\bar z_3)\) has no invariant complex lines; its invariant complex two-planes are identified with \(S^4\). The following page calls \(\sigma\) an involution.
statement: On \(\mathbb C^4\), this antilinear map satisfies \(\sigma^2=-1\). It therefore induces a fixed-point-free involution on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\). Its invariant two-planes are quaternionic lines, parametrized by \(\mathbb{HP}^1\simeq S^4\). Sending \([z]\) to \(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(z,\sigma z)\) is the twistor fibration with fiber \(\mathbb{CP}^1\).
fate: The twistor setting is already present in \citet{atiyahward1977instantons}; the precise real structure is written in \citet[\S0.2 and \S1.6]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. The latter is a detailed later exposition, not the first appearance of twistor space.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Affine coordinates of the twistor map
notes: Two complex quotients give \(x_2+ix_1\) and \(x_4+ix_3\), and a remark says that three coordinates suffice.
statement: On \((z_3,z_4)\ne(0,0)\), put \(x_2+ix_1=(z_1\bar z_3+\bar z_2z_4)/(|z_3|^2+|z_4|^2)\) and \(x_4+ix_3=(\bar z_2z_3-z_1\bar z_4)/(|z_3|^2+|z_4|^2)\). These are constant on the complex projective line associated with a quaternionic line. Three complex affine coordinates on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) suffice; the statement is not a claim that three real coordinates parametrize \(S^4\).
fate: \citet[\S1.6]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} print the coordinate construction in the detailed proof. It is an elementary coordinate expression of the earlier twistor map.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Self-duality as a type condition on pulled-back curvature
notes: The lemma says self-dual two-forms pull back to type \((1,1)\), while three complementary \((2,0)\) components are independent. Corollary (8) omits the component index on its bracket.
statement: For the indicated orientation, \(F=*F\) if and only if \((D^*F)^{2,0}=0\); for a unitary connection the conjugate \((0,2)\) condition follows. The three independent components detect the opposite-duality part. The condition \(D^*F=0\) without projection would force \(F=0\), since \(D\) is a surjective submersion.
fate: This is the local twistor criterion underlying \citet{atiyahward1977instantons} and made explicit in \citet[\S0.2 and \S1.6--1.9]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. The missing projection is a faithful notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Belavin’s covariant compatibility equations
notes: Belavin rewrites the criterion as commuting holomorphic covariant derivatives and then as \([L_1,L_2]=0\) for a spectral parameter \(\lambda\).
statement:
With \(
abla_\mu=\partial_\mu+A_\mu\), the pair \(L_1=\lambda(
abla_1-i
abla_2)+(
abla_3+i
abla_4)\), \(L_2=\lambda(
abla_3-i
abla_4)-(
abla_1+i
abla_2)\) has zero commutator for all \(\lambda\) exactly when the three self-duality equations hold in this convention. Equivalently the \((1,0)\) part of \(D^*
abla\) is flat in its holomorphic directions.
fate: \citet[\S1.6--1.9]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} use this compatibility and explicitly identify the Belavin--Zakharov route. Here the relative minus sign is retained; it differs from the problematic pair in the earlier Novikov notes.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.
speaker: A. A. Belavin

title: From a tensor subspace to the bundle fibers
notes: Choose \(I\subset H\otimes\mathbb C^4\), \(\dim I=n\). If \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) cut out a \(\sigma\)-invariant two-plane, take the orthogonal complement of \(I_{\ell_1}+I_{\ell_2}\).
statement: Write \(I_\ell=(1\otimes\ell)(I)\subset H\). For a quaternionic line \(D\subset\mathbb C^4\), let \(D^\circ\) be its annihilator and set \(L_D=(\sum_{\ell\in D^\circ}I_\ell)^\perp\). Choosing any basis \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) of \(D^\circ\) gives the same subspace, so the construction is independent of the two defining equations.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S3 and the unitary version in \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} supply the linear-algebra construction. The independence is immediate from linearity of contraction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Rank, positivity, and quaternionic orthogonality conditions
notes: Conditions 1 and 2 prescribe fiber dimension \(r\) and positivity. Condition 0 is inserted later as \(Q(I_\ell,I_{\ell\circ\sigma})=0\).
statement: Require the contraction sum over every quaternionic line to have rank \(2n\), take a positive Hermitian form on \(H\), and impose the quaternionic orthogonality constraint. Since \(\ell\circ\sigma\) is antilinear, the second contraction must use the complex-linear form \(z\mapsto\overline{\ell(\sigma z)}\). With these admissibility conditions the orthogonal complements form a smooth rank-\(r\) bundle and the projected connection is self-dual.
reconstruction: Positivity on the ambient Hermitian space is adopted as the convenient modern sufficient hypothesis. The source\textquotesingle s claim that positivity follows from its abbreviated conditions is not independently strengthened here.
fate: The admissibility and projection theorem are in \citet[\S2--\S4 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The detailed discussion of positivity appears in \citet[\S3--\S4]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. A bare indefinite form without the full conditions is insufficient.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Completeness and the equivalence relation on instanton data
notes: Theorem 1 says that the construction gives all self-dual Yang--Mills solutions and that nonisomorphic bundles correspond to inequivalent solutions. Isomorphisms of tensor diagrams are then described.
statement: Every regular unitary instanton on \(S^4\) is obtained from admissible finite-dimensional data. Two data sets yield gauge-equivalent connections precisely under the corresponding isomorphisms of diagrams, including an isometry on \(H\) and a change of basis in \(I\). The classification concerns bundles with connection; nonisomorphism of the underlying topological bundle is far too coarse.
fate: Exactly the completeness and uniqueness theorem of \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}, received 27 November 1977 and published in 1978; \citet[\S3]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} provide the fuller proof. The upper tensor factor in the notebook diagram needs \(\mathbb C^4\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The quadruple-of-subspaces intervention
notes: Gelfand invokes unpublished work with Ponomarev on quadruples with an automorphism. Ponomarev takes the four images of \(H\) in \((H^{\oplus4})/I\), then asks for the quadruples compatible with an orthogonal-complement operation.
statement: The quotient construction indeed associates four subspaces to a tensor inclusion. But the notes do not specify the additional automorphism, nondegeneracy hypotheses, duality functor or equivalence relation needed for the claimed Hermitian classification; no exact classification theorem can be reconstructed.
fate: \citet{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples} is the earlier complex quadruple-classification lead, received 21 October 1970 and published in 1971. Its metadata do not verify the additional unpublished Hermitian assertion. The instanton diagram theorem of \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} solves its own specified classification, not every possible quadruple-with-duality problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the extra unpublished assertion remains unidentified; the earlier quadruple work is thematic evidence only.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand and V. A. Ponomarev

title: Gram matrices and the absence of horizontal sections
notes: A basis of \(I\) produces \(4n\) vectors \(e_{ij}\in H\) and their Gram matrix \(\widetilde Q\). The assumption \(\operatorname{rank}\widetilde Q=2n+r\) is equated with absence of horizontal sections.
statement: For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), write the basis tensor as \(e_i=\sum_{j=1}^4e_{ij}\otimes f_j\). The Gram matrix determines these vectors up to unitary equivalence on their span. Full rank \(2n+r\) means they span \(H\). For the instanton data, failure of spanning gives a constant orthogonal summand and hence a flat factor; the converse uses the admissibility theorem.
fate: \citet[\S6--\S7]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} state the full-span criterion and the horizontal-section interpretation. The notebook\textquotesingle s basis endpoint \(e_r\) must be \(e_n\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The constrained four-by-four Gram blocks
notes: Every block has the displayed six-parameter pattern; Hermitian symmetry and rank are required, while Conditions 1 and 2 are expressly omitted.
statement: The block pattern is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&0&c&d\\0&a&e&f\\f&-d&b&0\\-e&c&0&b\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). It expresses the quaternionic orthogonality equations. Global Hermitian symmetry relates the block at \((k,\ell)\) to the adjoint of the block at \((\ell,k)\). Positivity and the pointwise rank conditions remain necessary; the linear block pattern alone does not classify regular instantons.
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} give the Gram-matrix formulation and explicitly acknowledge further regularity inequalities. Thus the notebook is an announcement of constraints, not an assertion that its listed linear equations suffice.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Affine generators of the orthogonal complement
notes: The vectors \(h_{k1}\) and \(h_{k2}\) are called \(2n\) global generators of \(L^\perp\) over \(S^4\), although their formulas use affine coordinates.
statement: On the chart \(\mathbb R^4\), the vectors \(h_{k1}=(x_2+ix_1)e_{k1}+(x_4-ix_3)e_{k2}+e_{k3}\) and \(h_{k2}=-(x_4+ix_3)e_{k1}+(x_2-ix_1)e_{k2}+e_{k4}\) span \(L_x^\perp\). They are not a global frame on \(S^4\) for nonzero charge: a rank-\(2n\) bundle globally generated by exactly \(2n\) independent sections would be trivial, contradicting \(c(L)c(L^\perp)=1\).
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} use these vectors in affine Euclidean coordinates. The local construction extends geometrically across infinity after changing trivialization, not by retaining one global affine frame.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Computing the connection from a kernel and orthonormal frame
notes: Solve \(2n\) homogeneous equations in \(2n+r\) variables, choose a fundamental system, orthonormalize, and differentiate to obtain \(A_\mu^{ij}=Q(\partial_\mu y^{(i)},y^{(j)})\).
statement: On a chart where a chosen minor is nonzero, solve \(Q(v,h_{ka}(x))=0\), \(k=1,\ldots,n\), \(a=1,2\), for a local basis of \(L_x\). Its coefficients are rational functions of the real coordinates. Gram--Schmidt introduces square roots of positive rational functions. If \(Y\) is the resulting orthonormal column frame, the connection matrix is \(Y^*dY\), up to the notebook\textquotesingle s transposed frame convention.
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} describe this explicit algorithm. Its formula is local and uses nonvanishing minors; no global rational orthonormal frame is implied.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The cohomological monad classification
notes: The final geometric theorem says diagrams classify bundles on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) satisfying \(H^i(L(-2))=0\), the same for \(L^*\), and \(H^2(L(-1))=H^0(L(-1))=0\); the range of \(i\) is not stated.
statement: A precise published version defines an admissible locally free sheaf \(E\) by \(H^i(E(k))=0\) for \(i=0,1\) with \(i+k\leq-1\), and for \(i=2,3\) with \(i+k\geq0\). The middle cohomology of a special monad \(0\to I\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H\otimes\mathcal O\to I^{\prime}\otimes\mathcal O(1)\to0\), with fiberwise injective and surjective end maps, gives an equivalence with admissible sheaves. Instantons additionally require the real and positivity conditions.
reconstruction: The full admissibility definition and monad exactness conditions are taken from the later theorem and are explicitly separated from the notebook\textquotesingle s abbreviated cohomology conditions.
fate: \citet[\S0.3--0.4 and Theorem~2.1]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} prove this equivalence; the paper was received 26 May 1978 and published in 1979. The short notebook vanishings are a precursor, not an independently complete list with all quantifiers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Hamiltonian formulation of a nonlinear scalar field
notes: The nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation is written with its Lagrangian, momentum \(\pi=u_t\), canonical bracket and energy.
statement: For a smooth real potential \(U(u)=m^2u^2/2+\varepsilon V(u)\), the formal Hamiltonian is \(H=\int[\pi^2/2+|\nabla u|^2/2+U(u)]\,dx\). The convention \(\{u(x),\pi(y)\}=\delta(x-y)\), \(u_t=\{u,H\}\), gives \(u_{tt}-\Delta u+U^{\prime}(u)=0\). Domain, boundary and regularity assumptions are needed for an actual infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian flow.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S1]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} give the sine-Gordon instance before the talk. The general variational identity is standard background.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Free-field Fock energy and occupation densities
notes: The free Hamiltonian is diagonalized by Fourier modes; the occupation density in (7) contains \(a^*(k^{\prime})a(k)\) and the energy is a sum of relativistic one-particle energies.
statement: After normal ordering, the free bosonic Hamiltonian is \(d\Gamma(\omega)\), \(\omega(k)=\sqrt{|k|^2+m^2}\). On generalized momentum states its energy is \(\sum_j\omega(k_j)\). The formal occupation density is \(a^*(k)a(k)\), or rigorously its smeared number operator; sharp-momentum states and delta-function occupations are distributions, not normalizable eigenvectors.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.148--149 of the Russian text]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} use exactly this particle interpretation. The prime on the first argument in the notebook is a scan-confirmed error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Nonspreading finite-energy solutions and failure of free scattering
notes: Solitons are first called everything failing to approach a free solution, then more narrowly finite-energy solutions that do not spread out.
statement: A localized stationary or traveling solution can obstruct scattering to a free Klein--Gordon wave. Non-scattering alone is not a definition of a soliton: it also includes other recurrent dynamics and, outside a global-existence class, breakdown of the solution. The intended soliton notion here is a localized coherent structure whose energy remains concentrated in a moving bounded region.
fate: \citet[introduction, pp.4--6]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} make the same distinction between spreading waves and localized structures; \citet[\S4]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} supply explicit sine-Gordon kinks and breathers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Lorentz boosts and the mass-shell relation
notes: Boosting a static finite-energy solution gives \(u_s((x-x_0-vt)/\sqrt{1-v^2})\) and \(H_s(v)=M/\sqrt{1-v^2}=\sqrt{p^2+M^2}\).
statement: For a localized static solution of a Lorentz-invariant scalar equation in one spatial dimension, a boost with \(|v|<1\) gives the displayed traveling profile. If \(M\) is its rest energy, the conserved energy-momentum vector gives \(E=M/\sqrt{1-v^2}\) and \(p=Mv/\sqrt{1-v^2}\). Boundary stress must vanish so the integrated charges transform correctly.
fate: \citet[\S1, equation~(2)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} state this explicitly for the sine-Gordon kink. The notebook\textquotesingle s schematic higher-dimensional opening does not turn the one-coordinate boost formula into a general \(d\)-dimensional expression.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Resolution into radiation and finitely many localized structures
notes: Equation (12) proposes \(u\to u_0+\sum u_s\) at large positive and negative time, calling it a hypothesis in general and a theorem in models. The next page explicitly adds periodic localized solutions.
statement: A precise model question is whether every global finite-energy sine-Gordon solution admits a large-time decomposition into finitely many localized coherent structures, including kinks, antikinks and breathers, plus radiation, in a specified topology. The notebook supplies neither a convergence norm nor genericity assumptions; it first writes a free-wave term and then explicitly adds periodic localized structures.
reconstruction: The all-energy sine-Gordon formulation makes the model and quantifiers explicit. The inclusion of breathers is supported by P000748; the exact radiation topology remains to be specified rather than attributed to the notebook.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1, Definition~2.6 and Theorem~10.1]{chenliulu2020sinegordon} prove resolution for generic data in \(H^{2,s}_{\sin}\times H^{1,s}\), \(s>1/2\); their radiation has modified scattering inside the light cone. The preprint first appeared 8 September 2020; the version read is 15 February 2022. This is a partial match to the unrestricted wording, not a theorem of free scattering for all energy data.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the cited generic weighted-data result is established. This search did not verify an all-finite-energy theorem matching the notebook wording. The verified theorem uses modified scattering for its radiation component.
worth: Worth developing in a carefully bounded form, because identifying the admissible coherent structures and the convergence topology prevents a false soliton-resolution assertion.

title: Additivity of asymptotic energies
notes: The notes pass from separated soliton asymptotics to \(H(u)=H(u_0)+\sum H_s(v_i)\).
statement: Energy additivity follows if the asymptotic decomposition converges strongly enough in the energy quantities and the interaction terms vanish as the localized profiles separate. Pointwise convergence alone is insufficient. In a long-range model the radiation energy may have a nonlinear scattering description even though its conserved energy is well-defined.
fate: \citet[introduction, equation~(1.13)]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} explicitly assume separation of the wave packet and localized solutions; \citet[\S4, equations~(32)--(33)]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} obtain an exact spectral energy decomposition in the integrable sine-Gordon setting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Several particle species from one classical field
notes: Quantization is expected to give sums of ordinary-particle and soliton energies, although only one scalar field occurs in the Lagrangian; soliton contributions persist in the classical limit.
statement: The semiclassical particle interpretation assigns species to stable localized classical solutions and their quantized internal excitations. In sine-Gordon the kink mass scales as inverse coupling. The displayed additive spectrum describes asymptotic multiparticle states; it is not a proof that an arbitrary nonlinear field has a rigorously constructed Fock decomposition or that all species are independent.
fate: \citet[\S1 and conclusion]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already formulate this semiclassical interpretation. In the exact sine-Gordon spectrum the lightest breather is identified with the perturbative neutral particle, so counting both as independent species would duplicate a state.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Periodic solitons and their internal parameters
notes: A periodic localized solution has center, velocity, period parameter \(\beta\) and initial phase \(\alpha\). Equation (18) then writes \(\sqrt{p_k^2+M(\alpha_k)}\).
statement: A breather has a frequency or action parameter controlling its rest energy and a separate phase parameter. Relativistic energy is \(\sqrt{p^2+M(\beta)^2}\) if \(\beta\) denotes that internal parameter. It is independent of the initial time phase. Thus (18) needs both the mass square and a parameter-name correction relative to the sentence immediately before it.
fate: \citet[\S1, equation~(3) and subsequent discussion]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} distinguish phase from the internal action and give the breather mass. Both defects in the notebook formula are visible in the scan.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Classical sine-Gordon kink and breather masses
notes: For \(u_{tt}-u_{xx}+m^2\sin u=0\), introducing coupling \(\gamma\) gives kink mass \(8m/\gamma\) and breather mass \((16m/\gamma)\sin\alpha\).
statement: Use \(H=\gamma^{-1}\int[\frac12u_t^2+\frac12u_x^2+m^2(1-\cos u)]dx\) and \(\{u(x),u_t(y)\}=\gamma\delta(x-y)\). The kink has energy \(8m/\gamma\). A breather with frequency \(m\cos\alpha\), \(0<\alpha<\pi/2\), has rest energy \((16m/\gamma)\sin\alpha\). The endpoint \(\alpha=\pi/2\) is a separatrix limit, not a finite-period breather.
fate: \citet[\S4]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} give these masses and explicit solutions; \citet[\S1]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} retain them. The source reverses the bracket order in (21) without changing its sign, unlike (3); the canonical convention is fixed here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Bohr--Sommerfeld breather levels and the exact coupling
notes: The internal angle is quantized as \(\alpha=\gamma n/16\), attributed approximately to Takhtajan--Faddeev, 1974.
statement: This is a semiclassical level rule with an upper bound on \(n\). In the exact sine-Gordon scattering convention with Lagrangian coupling \(\beta^2\), write \(\Gamma=\beta^2/(1-\beta^2/(8\pi))\). Bound-state masses satisfy \(m_n=2M\sin(n\Gamma/16)\), \(1\leq n<8\pi/\Gamma\). The bare or classical coupling must not silently be identified with \(\Gamma\).
fate: \citet[\S1 and \S5]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} discuss the semiclassical rule in 1975. \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} state the exact mass-ratio formula in May 1977. The notebook\textquotesingle s approximate 1974 attribution is not used to date the full quantum result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Rigorous construction of exponential interactions at small coupling
notes: Glimm, Jaffe and Fröhlich are invoked for rigorous small-coupling quantization, beside the expression \(m^2\gamma^{-1}(1-\cos\gamma u)\). Equation (26) writes \([\pi(x),u(y)]=i\delta(x-y)\), in the opposite order to the earlier Poisson bracket.
statement: Rigorous construction requires a specified normal ordering, ultraviolet limit, volume limit and normalization. The notebook\textquotesingle s potential has quadratic term \(m^2\gamma u^2/2\); it is not the canonically normalized potential \(m^2\beta^{-2}(1-\cos\beta\varphi)\) with small-oscillation mass \(m\). A theorem for a massive reference field is not automatically an identical theorem for every massless-reference sine-Gordon formulation.
reconstruction: With the convention used in item 1977-436.1, canonical quantization gives \([u(x),\pi(y)]=i\delta(x-y)\). The source changes the bracket order without specifying a corresponding sign convention.
fate: \citet[abstract]{froehlich1975quantized} announced a Wightman theory for a sine-Gordon interaction with a nonvanishing mass term in March 1975. The accessible primary abstract supports the historical construction claim, but does not verify every omitted hypothesis of the notebook\textquotesingle s Hamiltonian statement.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Short-range wave operators and a unitary scattering operator
notes: For \(H=-\Delta/(2m)+v\), with rapidly decaying \(v\), the double-time expression defines a unitary \(S\)-operator.
statement: For a real bounded short-range potential, for example \(|v(x)|\leq C\langle x\rangle^{-1-\epsilon}\), the wave operators \(W_\pm=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}\) exist and have range \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)\). Their completeness implies \(S=W_+^*W_-\) is unitary on the free Hilbert space. Bound states are not additional scattering channels; decay without self-adjointness assumptions is insufficient.
fate: The established short-range theorem is restated with proof in \citet[Theorem~2.4 and \S1]{yafaev2004lectures}, lectures delivered in 2001 and posted in 2004. This later exposition is used to check precise hypotheses, not to date the old scattering theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Extracting scattering amplitudes from propagator asymptotics
notes: Equations (30)--(31) evaluate the propagator along free classical rays and divide by free propagators to recover a momentum-space scattering kernel.
statement: The useful assertion is a distributional large-time extraction after testing against momentum wave packets and retaining the stationary-phase normalization. A pointwise quotient of kernels with omitted normalization is not, by itself, a well-defined equality for a scattering distribution. The required free rays are \(x=pt/m\).
reconstruction: Only the distributional, wave-packet interpretation is asserted here; the exact normalization cannot be recovered from the notebook\textquotesingle s formula alone.
fate: \citet[\S2.1, equations~(1.3)--(1.11)]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} present the corresponding prescription with its normalization and illustrate it by spectral expansion. The primary article was received 4 July 1977 and published in June 1978; the notebook\textquotesingle s ratio is an abbreviated precursor.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The stationary-phase exponent and amplitude
notes: Equation (32) gives \(\widetilde\Psi(mx/t)e^{ix^2/(2mt)}\) for an integral with phase \(px-p^2t/(2m)\).
statement: For the convention \(\Psi(x,t)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int\widehat\Psi(p)e^{i(px-p^2t/(2m))}dp\), \(m>0\), and Schwartz amplitude, the leading term as \(t\to+\infty\) on bounded velocity ranges is \(\sqrt{m/(2\pi t)}e^{-i\pi/4}e^{imx^2/(2t)}\widehat\Psi(mx/t)\). Both the mass position in the exponent and the power of \(t\) matter.
fate: This follows directly from the critical point \(p=mx/t\) and Hessian \(-t/m\). Compare \citet[equation~(2.8)]{yafaev2004lectures} in the normalization \(H_0=-\Delta\). The notebook error is faithfully transcribed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Path integrals with soliton boundary data
notes: Time-sliced mechanical and field path integrals are written, and sums of solitons are imposed as initial and final configurations to define transition quantities.
statement: These oscillatory path integrals encode propagators and, after asymptotic normalization, scattering amplitudes. They require regularization, renormalization and appropriate boundary conditions; an unqualified infinite product of Lebesgue measures does not define a continuum measure. A complex amplitude is not itself a transition probability.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already use this stationary-phase and renormalization scheme in 1975; \citet[\S2.2]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} develop the general soliton boundary prescription in the 1978 review.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: A quantum inverse-scattering method
notes: The notes say that there is not yet a good quantum version of the inverse problem.
statement: Construct quantum scattering-data operators and exchange relations that generate commuting quantum integrals and eigenstates for a specified integrable field model. This is a definite method problem when the model and operator algebra are fixed; it is not an existence theorem for every possible quantization.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S4]{sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum} give an early quantum inverse-scattering construction, received 28 July 1978 and published in December 1978. They explicitly construct the nonlinear-Schrödinger operators, while stating that the corresponding comparison with classical sine-Gordon variables had not yet been completed. Thus the early result has a precise model-dependent scope.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The exact sine-Gordon scattering matrix has two charge channels
notes: Zamolodchikov\textquotesingle s guessed exact formula is cited. Equation (46) then writes a single phase times momentum-conserving delta functions for a soliton and an antisoliton.
statement: The sine-Gordon two-particle matrix has transmission and reflection amplitudes in the soliton--antisoliton sector, with unitarity, crossing and prescribed bound-state poles. A single scalar phase describes an appropriate eigenchannel or reflectionless specialization; it is not the generic full charge-channel matrix.
fate: \citet{zamolodchikov1977exact} was received 4 January 1977 and published in June 1977. The separately opened primary announcement \citet[equations~(4)--(10)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp}, submitted 14 April and published 20 May 1977, explicitly displays both amplitudes. This was available before the talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Classical solvability versus quantum solvability
notes: The hypothesis says that every classically solvable problem is solvable in its quantum version.
statement: The source specifies neither solvability, quantization, preservation of integrals, domains, nor a class of models. Quantum anomalies and ordering choices are relevant to any precise formulation, so no universal yes-or-no proposition can be extracted without adding substantial hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S2]{sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum} provide a successful model construction, not a theorem that all classically integrable systems admit the required quantization. No exact fate is assigned to the unrestricted sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the general sentence remains under-specified. The precise quantum inverse-scattering method is treated separately.

title: The fluctuation determinant and the sine-Gordon zero mode
notes: Expanding around \(U_{cl}\) produces a Hessian and determinant. For a stationary soliton the notes give \(q(x)=1/\cosh^2x\), call it a Bargmann potential, and refer to a zero eigenfunction.
statement: For the sine-Gordon kink, the spatial Hessian is \(K=-\partial_x^2+m^2(1-2\operatorname{sech}^2(mx))\). Its translation mode \(u_s^{\prime}\) has eigenvalue zero. A determinant must remove this mode and account for the collective coordinate; the relevant object is a renormalized determinant ratio. The isolated positive \(\operatorname{sech}^2x\) is not this Hessian potential.
fate: \citet[\S2, equations~(12)--(18)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} explicitly exclude the zero mode, use the reflectionless spatial operator and express the determinant through spectral/scattering information. This is a precise earlier match after the source\textquotesingle s missing sign, coefficient and constant are restored.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Explicit higher-loop functionals of the resolvent kernel
notes: The next-loop discussion calls for \(R=A^{-1}\), its kernel, and \(\int R^3(x,x)\,d^2x\), with the hope that such quantities can be calculated explicitly.
statement: The expression is ambiguous between the diagonal of an operator cube and the cube of a coincident kernel; zero modes, boundary conditions, ultraviolet subtraction and counterterms are unspecified. It therefore does not define one finite invariant whose exact evaluation can be tracked.
fate: \citet[\S3 and \S4]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} discuss renormalized higher-loop diagrams and explicitly report their computational difficulty. This identifies the setting but not an exact value or theorem for the notebook\textquotesingle s ambiguous functional.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the displayed functional remains insufficiently specified; it is not entered as an allegedly untouched open problem.

title: The one-loop sine-Gordon mass correction
notes: The stated expansion is \(M=8m/\gamma-m/\pi+O(\gamma)\).
statement: In the semiclassical convention for weak sine-Gordon coupling, with renormalized mass parameter \(m_r\), the one-loop kink mass is \(M=8m_r/\gamma-m_r/\pi+O(\gamma)\). A finite renormalization of the mass parameter changes higher coefficients, so the symbol \(m\) must be specified when comparing schemes.
fate: \citet[\S2, following equation~(18), and \S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already give this result in 1975, with \(m_r\) the renormalized mass. The 1978 review is not its first publication.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The no-higher-corrections claim depends on the mass convention
notes: The notebook conjectures the exact identity \(M=8m/\gamma-m/\pi\), attributed to Zamolodchikov\textquotesingle s justification.
statement: Without defining the renormalized parameter \(m\), the all-orders statement is not determinate. For the physical lightest-breather mass \(m_1\) and the Lagrangian coupling \(g=\beta^2\), the exact ratio is \(M/m_1=[2\sin(\pi\xi/2)]^{-1}\), \(\xi=g/(8\pi-g)\). Its expansion is \(8/g-1/\pi+g/192+O(g^2)\), so the two-term expression is not exact in that physical-mass convention.
reconstruction: The Taylor expansion in the physical mass convention is an editorial algebraic consequence of the published ratio; it is not a claim that the notebook used that convention.
fate: The mass-ratio identity follows from \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp}. \citet[\S2--\S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} explicitly frame the earlier conjecture as the possibility that higher corrections reduce to renormalization. The source does not fix the convention needed to decide its literal all-orders wording.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the exact mass ratios are known in the specified sine-Gordon convention. The notebook\textquotesingle s bare claim cannot be labeled convention-independently true or false.

title: The coupling threshold is not simply soliton disappearance
notes: The last sentence says everything is fine for \(\gamma\leq8\pi\), beyond which the soliton disappears.
statement: The threshold \(\beta^2=8\pi\) concerns the quantum sine-Gordon interaction and its renormalization. It does not follow from extrapolating a one-loop mass to zero. Breather bound states already cease to exist when \(\xi\geq1\), equivalently \(\beta^2\geq4\pi\), while soliton and antisoliton scattering persist in the repulsive regime below \(8\pi\). Endpoint claims require separate hypotheses.
fate: \citet[abstract]{coleman1975equivalence} discuss unbounded energy density beyond \(8\pi\) in the stated convention; \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} distinguish the bound-state threshold. Neither supports the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted disappearance sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Semiclassical phase integrals and reflectionless couplings
notes: The abbreviated action gives an integral for the scattering phase. The notes replace it by a sum at \(\gamma=8\pi/N\) and describe interpolation to arbitrary coupling.
statement: The semiclassical phase is obtained from the two-soliton action after subtracting asymptotic external contributions. A finite-product exact scattering formula occurs at reflectionless values \(\Gamma=8\pi/N\), where \(\Gamma\) is the renormalized coupling of the exact scattering formula. In terms of \(\beta^2\), these values are \(8\pi/(N+1)\). A logarithm branch and analytic continuation must be fixed in the phase integral.
fate: \citet[\S4, equations~(27)--(30)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} derive the semiclassical phase; \citet[equations~(7)--(10)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} explicitly discuss the reflectionless interpolation. The notebook uses one symbol for distinct coupling conventions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The hyperbolic-secant scattering analogy
notes: Sine-Gordon scattering is said to resemble a Schrödinger problem in one space dimension \(-d^2/dx^2+a/\cosh^2(\alpha x)\); a possible eigenvalue formula is crossed out.
statement: This is an analogy with the explicitly solvable hyperbolic-secant potential. At special negative strengths \(a=-\ell(\ell+1)\alpha^2\), \(\ell\) a nonnegative integer, the Schrödinger potential is reflectionless. The notebook gives no parameter map identifying its entire Schrödinger spectrum with the quantum field theory, and the deleted eigenvalue is not restored as a theorem.
fate: The exact reflectionless fluctuation operator in \citet[\S2, equation~(16)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} and reflectionless quantum scattering in \citet[equation~(7)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} explain the comparison. They do not identify a literal equivalence of the two Hamiltonians.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The constrained sphere sigma model and its classical Lax representation
notes: The closing example is \(n:\mathbb R^{1,1}\to S^n\), with Lagrangian \(\frac12\int\partial n\cdot\partial n\,dx\), and a Lax pair attributed to Pohlmeyer and to Zakharov--Mikhailov.
statement: For a unit vector field \(n\in S^n\), the constrained Euler--Lagrange equation is \(\Box n+(\partial_\mu n\cdot\partial^\mu n)n=0\). Its nonlinearity comes from the constraint. The classical sphere sigma models admit a spectral-parameter zero-curvature formulation and conserved quantities; this does not by itself construct their quantum theory.
fate: \citet{pohlmeyer1976integrable} appeared in 1976, received 28 August 1975. \citet[introduction, \S3 and \S6]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic}, submitted 4 January 1978 and published June 1978, explicitly identify Pohlmeyer\textquotesingle s sphere-model result and develop the reduction and integration scheme. Thus the classical claim was already known; the latter article is not treated as a theorem of integrability for all homogeneous spaces.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Massive sigma-model particles scatter like solitons
notes: The scan reads \ru{Массивные частицы рассеиваются как солитоны}; both transcriptions instead say that particles appear as solitons.
statement: The intended comparison is elastic, factorized scattering of massive quantum particles: multiparticle amplitudes are assembled from two-particle amplitudes, with no particle production in the integrable description. It is not a claim that all these particles are classical topological kink solutions.
reconstruction: The reading of the Russian verb was checked independently against the scan by both this record editor and the chapter assembler.
fate: \citet[\S1--\S3]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on} construct an \(O(N)\)-invariant factorized matrix for \(N\geq3\) and support its sigma-model identification by perturbative comparisons, expressly distinguishing that identification from the algebraic construction. The article was received 22 August 1977, revised 14 November 1977, and published in February 1978. This closely matches the scattering remark but is not a proof of a fully axiomatized field theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Topoi and derived categories as organizing concepts
notes: I. M. Gelfand singles out the topos and the derived category as two primary categorical concepts.
statement: This is a methodological comparison, not a classification or universal-property theorem: a topos organizes sheaf-theoretic localization, while a derived category records complexes up to quasi-isomorphism.
reconstruction: The explanatory distinction is editorial; the notebook only lists the two concepts.
fate: The latter framework was already developed in the Harvard seminar of 1963--1964, published as \citet[Chapter~I]{hartshorne1966residues}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is exposition of this result.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Graded exterior modules and evaluation complexes
notes: \(\Lambda=\Lambda(\Xi)\), \(\dim\Xi=n+1\), \(\deg\xi_i=-1\), and \(V=\bigoplus V_j\) is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any \(0\ne\xi\in\Xi\) makes \(\cdots\to V_1\to V_0\to V_{-1}\to\cdots\) a complex because \(\xi^2=0\).
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), the exterior algebra of an \((n+1)\)-dimensional vector space has \(\dim\Lambda_{-k}=\binom{n+1}{k}\). For a finite graded left module, the maps \(v\mapsto\xi v\) have degree \(-1\) and square zero. A module is called proper here when its evaluation complex has homology only in degree zero for every nonzero \(\xi\).
fate: The same definitions precede Theorem~1 of \citet{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}; submitted 10 January 1978, published in Russian later in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: Constant rank and the bundle of evaluation homology
notes: For proper \(V\), \(\dim H_0(L_\xi(V))\) is constant by the Euler characteristic; these spaces form a bundle.
statement: For a finite complex with all fiber homology except degree zero vanishing, the remaining dimension is the alternating sum of the dimensions of the terms, hence is independent of the projective point. The cohomology sheaf of the associated locally free complex is locally free and commutes with taking fibers.
reconstruction: The local-freeness and base-change assertion is stated explicitly here; a constant Euler characteristic by itself would not suffice without the other fiber cohomology vanishing.
fate: This is the well-definedness step for \(\Phi(V)\) in \citet[Section~3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: Free exterior modules produce the zero bundle
notes: The regular module and its shifts have zero evaluation homology. The subsequent sentence says that free modules give a \ru{тривиальное расслоение}.
statement: For \(0\ne\xi\), choose \(\ell\in\Xi^*\) with \(\ell(\xi)=1\); contraction by \(\ell\) contracts multiplication by \(\xi\). Thus every finite graded free \(\Lambda\)-module gives an acyclic complex, hence the rank-zero bundle, not an arbitrary positive-rank trivial bundle.
reconstruction: The contraction proof and explicit rank-zero wording clarify the notebook. No new theorem is claimed.
fate: Acyclicity of free modules is used in \citet[Section~3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: Stable exterior-module description of algebraic vector bundles
notes: Every algebraic bundle is \(\Phi(V)\), and \(\Phi(V)\cong\Phi(V')\) iff \(V\oplus P\cong V'\oplus P'\) for free modules. The notes credit Bernstein and both Gelfands, and mention an independent related result of Beilinson.
statement: For \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\), isomorphism classes of algebraic vector bundles are in bijection with stable isomorphism classes of finite graded proper \(\Lambda(\mathbb C^{n+1})\)-modules. Stabilization is by finite sums of grading shifts of the regular module.
fate: Exact match: \citet[Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}. This is a reduction to module classification, not a list of all bundle moduli.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: The twisting sheaf and its local rank-one property
notes: Three definitions of \(O(j)\) are offered: transition functions, homogeneous degree-\(j\) rational functions, and powers of the anti-Hopf bundle. An exercise asks why the resulting bundle is one-dimensional.
statement: For a Zariski-open \(U\subset\mathbb P^n\), sections of \(O(j)\) are homogeneous rational functions of degree \(j\) regular on the inverse image of \(U\) in \(\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}\). On \(x_i\ne0\), multiplication by \(x_i^{-j}\) identifies this module with \(O_U\), proving local rank one. Negative powers mean dual tensor powers.
reconstruction: The topology and omission of the cone vertex are necessary. Regular algebraic sections, rather than arbitrary analytic sections, are intended.
fate: The twisting sheaves and homogeneous-module construction are classical: \citet[Chapter~III]{serre1955coherent}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; the notebook is exposition of this result.

title: The linear sheaf complex associated with an exterior module
notes: \(\mathcal L^j=V_{-j}\otimes O(j)\) and \((df)(\xi)=\xi f(\xi)\).
statement: The tautological section defines maps \(V_{-j}\otimes O(j)\to V_{-j-1}\otimes O(j+1)\). The exterior relations give \(d^2=0\); the construction is independent of a basis of \(\Xi\).
fate: This is precisely \(L(V)\) in \citet[Section~3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: A truncated Koszul kernel followed by syzygies
notes: The page starts mid-proof: \(C_N\otimes\Lambda\to C_{N+1}\otimes\Lambda\), \(c\otimes\lambda\mapsto\sum X_i(c)\otimes\xi_i\lambda\); take its kernel and then \(N\) free-kernel steps with grading shifts.
statement: If \(C\) is a graded module over \(S=\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\), multiplication by the coordinate functions gives the displayed basis-independent linear map. For sufficiently high truncation and suitable grading conventions, a Koszul-dual module may be recovered using successive syzygies.
reconstruction: The missing preceding P000755 is not attached. C, the admissible bound on N, and the exact shift cannot be recovered from P000756 alone; no unique explicit inverse is asserted.
fate: The structural inverse belongs to the BGG equivalence, \citet[Theorem~2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}; this page's precise normalization is only partially matched.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the stated construction is established; the qualifications above are essential.

title: Serre's quotient-category description of coherent sheaves
notes: Gelfand urges replacing bundles by sheaves, since bundles do not form an abelian category. Coherent sheaves on projective space correspond to finitely generated graded polynomial modules modulo finitely many components.
statement: For \(S=\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\), sheafification induces \(\operatorname{grmod}(S)/\operatorname{tors}(S)\simeq\operatorname{Coh}(\mathbb P^n)\), where torsion means finite-dimensional graded modules. A representative is \(\bigoplus_{j\ge N}H^0(\mathcal E(j))\) for sufficiently large \(N\).
reconstruction: Truncation avoids claiming the unbounded section module is finitely generated for every coherent sheaf; e.g. a skyscraper has sections in every negative twist.
fate: \citet[Chapter~III]{serre1955coherent} is the relevant 1955 publication; the notebook's 1953 bibliographic date is inaccurate.

title: The complete-flag double fibration
notes: Beilinson considers full flags in four-space, projecting to \(G(4,2)\) by forgetting the line and hyperplane, and to \(Q\subset\mathbb P^3\times\mathbb P^{3*}\) by forgetting the plane.

title: Parallel sections along null curves and descent
notes: A bundle with connection on the Grassmannian is canonically trivial along each CP1 because curvature vanishes in dimension 1 and the fundamental group is zero. Pull back to F, descend to Q, and obtain a holomorphic bundle trivial on CP1 times CP1.
statement: For a holomorphic connection, curvature is a holomorphic2-form and its restriction to a complex curve vanishes. On a simply connected curve, parallel sections identify the bundle with its space of horizontal sections tensored with its structure sheaf; there is no distinguished basis of that space. On an admissible complex open region, the spaces of sections along null curves form the descended bundle, provided the fibers are connected and simply connected and the analytic descent hypotheses hold. A smooth real connection does not have zero curvature merely because the curve has complex dimension 1.

fate: This is the parallel-section construction of \citet[Section~2, Theorem~1 and footnote~1]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. The2005 preprint/2006 publication restates the 1978 correspondence; it is not evidence of a new1979 theorem by the adjacent speaker.

title: The reverse ambitwistor correspondence and missing field equations

title: Grading and transitivity in the adjoint action
notes: A graded Lie algebra has \([\mathfrak g_i,\mathfrak g_j]\subset\mathfrak g_{i+j}\). The bracket gives maps to \(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathfrak g_{-1},\mathfrak g_{i-1})\) and \(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathfrak g_1,\mathfrak g_{i+1})\), assumed injective in opposite degree ranges.

The stated injectivity means that a nonnegative-degree element centralizing \(\mathfrak g_{-1}\), or a nonpositive-degree element centralizing \(\mathfrak g_1\), is zero. For the classification discussed later one also imposes finite-dimensional homogeneous pieces, appropriate generation and irreducibility, and a characteristic-zero algebraically closed ground field.

title: Four Cartan families and the missing classification hypotheses

title: The maximal Cartan prolongation and Jacobi symmetry
notes: For depth 1, the notes say the whole algebra is recovered from \(\mathfrak g_{-1},\mathfrak g_0\), and define successive symmetric maps by the Jacobi identity.
statement: Let V be finite-dimensional and \(\mathfrak h\subset\mathfrak{gl}(V)\). Its maximal prolongation has \(\mathfrak g_{-1}=V\), \(\mathfrak g_0=\mathfrak h\), and \[\mathfrak g_k=(S^{k+1}V^*\otimes V)\cap(S^kV^*\otimes\mathfrak h),\quad k\ge1.\] The symmetry of \(f(v_1,\ldots,v_k)v_{k+1}\) follows from the Jacobi identity and \([V,V]=0\). Every transitive algebra with these lower pieces embeds in the prolongation; equality is a maximality condition, not automatic.

fate: The construction is spelled out in \citet[Section~2.2]{ottazziwarhurst2011contact}, which treats it as the classical Singer--Sternberg prolongation; its earlier history includes \citet{guilleminquillensternberg1967infinite}.

Transitivity gives uniqueness, and the symmetry conditions yield existence and Jacobi. Equivalently use the commutator of their polynomial-vector-field realizations. The phrase most finite-dimensional is heuristic, not a measure-theoretic genericity theorem.

title: The polynomial vector-field realization

title: The complex rank-one criterion for infinite type
notes: Wilson's lemma: the Cartan prolongation is infinite-dimensional iff some \(\xi\in\mathfrak g_0\) has rank 1; the speaker refers to Guillemin and two coauthors. Reductivity and irreducibility are separately mentioned.

title: Generalized Cartan matrices and symmetrizability
notes: A has diagonal2, nonpositive integer off-diagonal entries with simultaneous zeros, and can be made symmetric by \(n_{\alpha\beta}\mapsto n_{\alpha\beta}\lambda_\alpha/\lambda_\beta\). An invariant form is then mentioned.

The associated symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra admits the standard invariant symmetric form, with the usual qualification on its center or full Cartan realization.

title: Root-lattice and height gradings
notes: The fine grading has degrees \(-\alpha,0,\alpha\) on \(f_\alpha,h_\alpha,e_\alpha\), and the coarse grading degrees \(-1,0,1\). Nonzero degrees with a nonzero component are roots; nonnegative simple-root combinations are called positive.

A root is a nonzero \(\gamma\in Q\) with nonzero root space, and a positive root lies in \(Q_+\setminus\{0\}\). Not every nonnegative integral combination is a root.

title: Finite, affine, and indefinite growth
notes: Positive definite A gives a finite-dimensional algebra; semidefinite singular A gives growth1 with uniformly bounded graded dimensions; a negative eigenvalue is said to give exponential growth. The type-A chain matrix gives sl(n+1).

title: The center from the kernel of the Cartan matrix

title: Untwisted loop algebras and the missing central quotient
notes: The first affine rank-two matrix is said to give \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\otimes\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]\); more generally use any finite-dimensional g, with the extra generators obtained from the longest root vectors times \(t^{\pm1}\).

title: Twisted loop algebras from an involution
notes: For \(\tau^2=1\), decompose \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g_+\oplus\mathfrak g_-\) and take even powers with \(\mathfrak g_+\), odd with \(\mathfrak g_-\). The example is \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\), \(\tau(X)=-X^T\).

title: A one-dimensional graded bracket with period three
notes: There are generators \(\varepsilon_i\), \(i\in\mathbb Z\), and \([\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j]=a_{ij}\varepsilon_{i+j}\), where \(a_{ij}\in\{-1,0,1\}\) is congruent to \(j-i\pmod3\). It is called simple.

For \([h,e]=2e,[h,f]=-2f,[e,f]=h\), one realization is \(\varepsilon_{3r}=\tfrac12ht^r\), \(\varepsilon_{3r+1}=et^r\), \(\varepsilon_{3r-1}=\tfrac12ft^r\). It is graded-simple in the intended sense; it is not simple as an ungraded Lie algebra, since \((t-1)\mathfrak{sl}_2[t,t^{-1}]\) is a nonzero proper ideal.

title: Hermitian matrices, spinors and the Lorentz cover
notes: A real four-vector is the Hermitian matrix \(X=x^0I+x^i\sigma_i\); its determinant is the Lorentz metric, and \(X\mapsto A^*XA\) gives the Lorentz action. Two Weyl spinor representations are used.

title: The real N=1 super-Poincare algebra
notes: Ten even generators P,L and four real spinorial odd generators satisfy \(\{Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta}\}=2\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_m\), \(\{Q,Q\}=\{\bar Q,\bar Q\}=0\), and \([P,Q]=0\); dimension is written(10,4).
